headline: Reliance Communications initiates Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Reliance Communications Limited has filed for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, notifying the NSE of the formal commencement of insolvency proceedings.
implication: CIRP trigger signals that RCOM's liabilities exceed ability to service debt; all suspended operations must navigate operational creditor hierarchy and resolution plan submission timelines under IBBI rules, requiring lenders and stakeholders to file claims within statutory windows.
detail: Reliance Communications Limited, a major telecom operator, has initiated a formal Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, marking a critical juncture for its creditors, operational continuity and asset recovery. The company disclosed the CIRP filing to the NSE, triggering regulatory notification requirements. The resolution process will proceed under IBC 2016 rules, with NCLT oversight and IBBI-prescribed timelines for claim settlement, resolution plan submission and stakeholder voting.

conditions: NCLT admission order (prerequisite for CIRP commencement)
IRP appointment and CoC constitution within statutory timeline
Filing of claims by financial and operational creditors within stipulated period
Resolution plan submission and approval via CoC vote (minimum 66% by value)
approvals: NCLT admission and CIRP order (under IBC Section 7)
IBBI oversight of IRP conduct and timeline compliance
NSE/BSE notification under SEBI LODR Regulation 30 (done)

triggers.note: CIRP triggered by either creditor petition (if RCOM in default >180 days) or debtor petition; NCLT must admit and appoint IRP
Moratorium automatically applies; all recovery suits and property attachment frozen; all contracts voidable at IRP discretion
Listed entity (RCOM on NSE/BSE) must disclose CIRP as material event within 24 hours of knowledge
Sets resolution period (120/180 days), claim submission window, IRP eligibility, CoC procedures, and plan approval mechanism
